title: Exploring Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud Detection from a Philippine Perspective
authors: Blancaflor, E.; Asuncion, K. D.; Reyes, H. J.; Verzosa, M.
venue: 2024 The 6th World Symposium on Software Engineering (WSSE)
tldr: Literature review of ML techniques for credit card fraud detection in the Philippines, comparing SVM, ANN, KNN, Naive Bayes, and Logistic Regression, finding ANN-SMOTE achieves superior performance.
problem_and_motivation: Credit card fraud in the Philippines surged 21% since the COVID-19 pandemic, with online fraud costing consumers over P540 million in 2021 alone. Traditional fraud prevention systems are inadequate against evolving threats.
approach: Systematic literature review of ML techniques for credit card fraud detection in the Philippine context.
Examines five core algorithms: Logistic Regression, KNN, Naive Bayes, SVM, and ANN.
Reviews enhanced variants including GA-based and SMOTE-based model enhancements.
Evaluates models using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, MCC, and BCR metrics.
Synthesizes findings from prior comparative studies to assess relative model performance.
findings: num: 21% increase in fraudulent credit card operations in the Philippines since the pandemic.
num: P540 million in online fraud losses in 2021 according to BSP.
num: Naive Bayes achieved 97.92% accuracy in comparative fraud detection studies.
ANN-SMOTE outperformed all other models on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score.
num: Logistic Regression achieved only 54.86% accuracy.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: Comparative performance of ML models (ANN vs LR with GA and SMOTE) -> ANN-SMOTE shows best accuracy, precision, recall, and F1.
Table 1: Five ML models evaluated with accuracy and improvement strategies -> ANN up to 98.44%, Logistic Regression only 54.86%.
